diagnostic_evidence.quote: we test the influence of the stabilization parameters $\sigma^E$ and $\tau^E$ on the convergence of eigenvalues of \eqref{a3.3} by setting the values of $\sigma^E$ and $\tau^E$ as $10^{-3}, 10^{-2}, 10^{-1}, 10^{1}, 10^{2}, 10^{3}$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: Positivity of the two gradient coefficients produced by the Young splitting requires epsilon_4 > c^*/(gamma c_*) and epsilon_4 < c_*/c^*, i.e. (c^*/c_*)^2 < gamma. Assumptions (a3.7)-(a3.8) only give c_* = min(1,c_0), c^* = max(1,c_1), so c^*/c_* is unrestricted (and is about 10^3 for the stabilization values tested in Section 4). Hence the asserted epsilon_4 generally does not exist and (a3.9) is unproved for the stated class of stabilizations; the case 1/gamma>1 ("Similarly") has the same defect, needing (c^*/c_*)^2 < 1/gamma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the cross term by |a_h^E(psi_h,phi_h)| <= (a_h^E(psi_h,psi_h) a_h^E(phi_h,phi_h))^{1/2} and use positive definiteness of the 2x2 form [[1,-1/gamma],[-1/gamma,1/gamma]] (resp. [[1,-1],[-1,1/gamma]]), then conclude with (a3.7); the same works for every admissible stabilization.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete inf-sup/well-posedness argument for (a3.5) and all subsequent source-problem and eigenvalue error estimates lose their justification for general admissible stabilizations.
issues.title: Weak T-coercivity of a_h rests on an epsilon choice that need not exist
issues.why_classification: A single local estimate swap proves (a3.9) for all stabilizations allowed by (a3.7)-(a3.8); every claim, rate and regime survives with no new lemma or construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: by Fredholm's alternative we conclude that the problem \eqref{a3.5} is well-posed.

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims to solve for the pair (U_h,k_h^2) from a_h(U_h,Psi_h)=0, but k_h^2 never occurs in this equation because a_h was defined with the fixed wave number k; so k_h^2 is undetermined and (a3.10) does not define the asserted approximation. The quoted sentence then asserts simultaneously that k_h^2 is "not an eigenvalue of (a3.10)" (although (a3.10) is presented as the eigenvalue problem whose eigenvalue is k_h^2) and that k_h^2 converges to k^2, while k^2 is assumed not to be an eigenvalue of (2.9). Fredholm's alternative for (a3.5) needs exactly the injectivity of the homogeneous discrete problem at the given k^2, which none of these statements establishes.

failure_location.quote: Since \(k^2\) is not an eigenvalue of \eqref{a2.9}, it is known that for sufficiently small \(h\), \(k_h^2\) is also not an eigenvalue of \eqref{a3.10} and $k_h^2$ converges to $k^2$ (see \cite{MengMei2022}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define (a3.10) as an eigenvalue problem in the parameter (replace k^2 by k_h^2 in a_h), invoke convergence of its spectrum to that of (2.9) to conclude that the homogeneous discrete problem at the fixed k^2 has only the zero solution for small h, and then apply Fredholm's alternative to get the inf-sup stability of (a3.5).
issues.overall_effect: The discrete solution operator A_h (and therefore the whole discrete error analysis) is left without a valid well-posedness argument for (a3.5).
issues.title: Well-posedness of the discrete source problem is justified via an ill-defined problem (a3.10)
issues.why_classification: The conclusion (well-posedness of (a3.5) for small h) is correct and follows from a short standard injectivity-plus-Fredholm argument; no claim or rate is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: &= a_h({\bf U}^{\bf F}_h-{ f U}^{\bf F}_{\pi},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_I-{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi) - a({\bf U}^{\bf F}_h-{ f U}^{\bf F}_{\pi},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_I-{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi)  + a_h({\bf U}^{\bf F}_{h},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi) - a({\bf U}^{\bf F}_{h},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi).

issues.failure_explanation: For a polynomial p and a general v_h the stiffness and the beta k^2-mass terms cancel exactly, but the n-mass term does not: a_h(p,v_h)-a(p,v_h) = -k^2 sum_E b^E(n p_1 - Pi^0(n p_1), (I-Pi^0)v_{h,1}), which is zero only when n is (piecewise) polynomial. This quantity is nevertheless recorded as "-0" in Lemma 3.4's proof and is silently dropped in the identity used in Lemma 3.3's proof, which likewise requires a_h(U^F_pi,.) = a(U^F_pi,.).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the zero by |k^2 sum_E b^E(n p_1-Pi^0(n p_1),(I-Pi^0)v_{h,1})| \lesssim \|n p_1-\Pi^0(n p_1)\|_0\|v_h-\Pi^0 v_h\|_0 \lesssim h^{1+\min(l,s)}\|w^f\|_{1+\min(l,s)}\|v_h\|_0, which is absorbed by the right-hand sides of (a3.16) and (a3.20), or reorganise the splitting so that only polynomial arguments appear in the second slot.
issues.overall_effect: For non-polynomial refractive index n the source-problem estimates (a3.16) and (a3.20) are unproved as written (they remain true once the dropped term is estimated).
issues.title: Consistency of a_h with a polynomial in the first slot is wrongly set to zero
issues.why_classification: One local estimate replaces the erroneous zero (or a simplified splitting avoids it); both lemma statements and all advertised rates survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, \((\beta - \lambda)\) is an eigenvalue of \eqref{a2.3} if and only if \(\mu\) is an eigenvalue of \({\bf \mathcal{A}}\) where \(\mu = \frac{1}{\beta - \lambda}\).
Let $R(\lambda_j)$ be the space spanned by the eigenfunctions of $T$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda_j$,
$R_{h}(\lambda_{j})$ be the direct sum of the eigenspaces corresponding to the eigenvalues of $T_{h}$ that converge to $\lambda_j$

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own relation mu = 1/(beta-lambda), T u_j = mu_j u_j with mu_j = 1/(beta-lambda_j), which is not lambda_j in general; this contradicts the quoted assertion and makes R(lambda_j), R_h(lambda_j), R^*, R_h^* the wrong (generically empty) spectral clusters. The Babuška-Osborn estimate used in (a3.28) applies to T and therefore bounds |mu_j - mu_hat_{j,h}|, not |lambda_j - lambda_hat_{j,h}|; the eigenvalue bound (a3.23) is not obtained as written.

failure_location.quote: Obviously, if \((\lambda_j, {\bf U}_j=(w_j,u_j))\) is an eigenpair of \(\eqref{a2.3}\), then \((\lambda_j, u_j)\) is an eigenpair of \(T\);

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Relabel the T-spectrum by mu_j = 1/(beta-lambda_j) (or replace T by beta I - T^{-1}, whose eigenvalues are exactly lambda_j) and transfer the averaged eigenvalue bound back through lambda = beta - 1/mu, using |mu_{i,h}-mu_j| = O(h^{min(l,s)}) to control the nonlinearity of the averaging.
issues.overall_effect: (a3.22) refers to the wrong eigenspaces and the derivation of the eigenvalue estimate (a3.23) is invalid; the eigenfunction estimates of thm:added-1 inherit the mislabelled clusters through (a3.27) and (a3.33).
issues.title: Eigenvalues of T are 1/(beta-lambda), not lambda: spectral clusters and (a3.28) misidentified
issues.why_classification: All statements and rates survive, but the spectral bookkeeping and the whole eigenvalue step must be rebuilt with a contained change-of-variable argument; no global architecture or regime is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The operator A_h is defined by a_h(A_h F,Psi_h) = b(F,Psi_h) but is identified with U_h^F, the solution of (a3.5), which uses b_h; the two objects differ. The quoted identity holds only for the b-based discrete operators (it needs b(U_h^f,F^*) = b(F,U_h^{f^*})), while Lemmas 3.3-3.4 analyse the b_h-based problem; for that problem the identity is off by [b-b_h](U_h^f,F^*) - [b-b_h](F,U_h^{f^*}), which is not zero. With the b-based reading, on the other hand, Lemmas 3.3-3.4 do not apply to A_h.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define A_h and A_h^* through b_h (consistent with (a3.5), (a3.12)) and add the missing consistency terms |[b-b_h](U_h^f,F^*)| + |[b-b_h](F,U_h^{f^*})| \lesssim h^{2+\min(l,s)} to the bound of I+II+III.
issues.overall_effect: The splitting I+II+III that bounds the first term of (a3.28) is invalid for the discrete problem actually analysed, so (a3.23) is unproved as written.
issues.title: Discrete solution operator defined with b while (a3.5) uses b_h; key identity for (a3.23) fails
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the operator definition plus one extra consistency estimate of the size already claimed preserves the statement and rate of (a3.23).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From the continuity of \(a(\cdot, \cdot)\) and the error estimate in the sense of \({\bf \mathds{V}}\) norm for the source problem

issues.failure_explanation: All three quantities I, II, III contain (A^*-A_h^*)F^* with F^* = (0,xi_i^*) built from adjoint eigenvectors. Bounding them by h^{min(l,s)} requires (by Lemma 3.4 applied to (a3.12)) the adjoint source solutions to lie in H^{1+s} x H^{1+s} and the adjoint eigenvectors to have matching regularity. The statement hypothesises H^{1+s} only for the primal eigenspace M(lambda_j); for complex n the adjoint problem is the problem for the coefficient n-bar, so its regularity does not follow from that hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis M^*(lambda_j^*) subset H^{1+s} x H^{1+s} (equivalently H^{1+s}-regularity of the adjoint source solutions with adjoint eigenfunctions as data) and apply Lemma 3.4 to (a3.12) as for the primal problem.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue rate (a3.23), |lambda_j - lambda_hat_{j,h}| \lesssim h^{2 min(l,s)}, is unsupported in the non-self-adjoint regime (e.g. Setting 2 with n = 2+4i) unless adjoint regularity is added.
issues.title: Theorem 3.1 omits the adjoint-regularity hypothesis its proof needs
issues.why_classification: Adding this standard local regularity condition restores the claimed rate with no change to the method, the conclusion or the rate, and only marginally narrows the covered problems.
